topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Hallmarks and Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by outlining the learning objectives and introducing Hanahan and Weinberg's hallmarks of cancer framework.

topics.label: Deregulated Signaling Pathways Driving Proliferation and Survival
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how mutations in cell-surface receptors and intracellular signaling cascades, such as Wnt, RTK/Ras/MAPK, PI3K/Akt, and TGF-beta, confer growth-signal autonomy and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation Blocks in Tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer cells undergo differentiation arrest, preventing terminal maturation and trapping cells in a proliferative state across hematopoietic and intestinal tissues.

topics.label: Evasion of Apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic focuses on how cancer cells resist programmed cell death through mutations in p53 and shifts in the balance between pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins such as Bax and Bcl-2.

topics.label: Replicative Immortality and Senescence Bypass
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells overcome the Hayflick limit via telomerase reactivation and bypass normal p53-mediated stress responses that enforce cell cycle arrest and senescence.

topics.label: Metabolic Reprogramming and Onco-Metabolites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce complex cancer hallmarks and explain how tumor cells rewire cellular metabolism through aerobic glycolysis, Krebs cycle enzyme mutations, and epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Tumor Angiogenesis and the Angiogenic Switch
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the requirement for new blood vessel growth to sustain tumor oxygenation and examine how the balance of pro- and anti-angiogenic signals controls vessel formation during progression.

topics.label: The Metastatic Cascade and Secondary Colonization
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic analyzes the biological mechanisms of cancer metastasis, including invasion, vascular transit, organ tropism, and the genomic features underlying metastatic survival.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Future Perspectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing of the lecture, summarizing the hallmark paradigm, pointing to recent literature extensions, and inviting questions.
